title: Hybrid Burst Credit Model and Time-Decay Exemptions PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview:
This PRD defines a new hybrid burst credit model paired with a time-decayed exemptions mechanism for plan entitlements and overage billing. The goal is to give customers predictable baseline quotas, short-term burst capability, and a principled way to admit transient overage without punitive immediate charges while keeping revenue integrity and clear invoiceability.

Why now:
- Increasing number of customers hit short-lived spikes (e.g., product launches, marketing events) and request predictable short bursts without manual support.
- Current soft-overage policies are either too lenient (manual credits) or too aggressive (instant overage invoices) causing poor UX and reconciliation burden.
- Dedicated and Hosted customers expect different fairness guarantees; this model seeks a single configurable abstraction.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce manual credit support tickets related to bursts by 60% within first quarter after rollout.
- Keep net monthly overage revenue variance within +/-3% of forecasts (no unexpected write-downs).
- Ensure 99.9% accuracy in billing statements with burst-credit usage attribution.

Non-goals:
- This does not change base plan pricing or base tokens-per-plan.
- Not introducing per-token dynamic pricing changes in this phase.

Model design (high level):
1) Baseline quota: each plan keeps its existing monthly token quota expressed as "baseline units."
2) Burst credit pool: each account receives a burst pool (hours or token-equivalent) sized depending on plan and historical volatility. Pool renews monthly but can be topped during commit changes.
3) Time-decayed exemptions: when a customer consumes burst credits and exceeds baseline + burst, they enter an exemption window (configurable, default 72 hours) during which overage charges are withheld or discounted and the system records metadata for reconciliation. Exemption magnitude decays linearly over the window (e.g., 100% exemption at t=0 down to 0% at t=end).
4) Priority segmentation: burst consumption is tagged by caller/route so critical routes (payment flows, admin actions) can be exempted from decay or draw from a reserved priority bucket.
5) Reconciliation phase: at the end of the exemption window or month, usage that remained in exemption is either billed at discounted overage rates or recharged against purchased credits depending on account settings and thresholds.

Configuration surface (exposed to Console/API):
- burst_pool_size: integer (tokens)
- exemption_window_hours: integer (default 72)
- decay_curve: enum [linear, exponential] (default linear)
- priority_buckets: list of route tags and bucket allocations
- auto_charge_on_end: boolean (invoice immediately vs accumulate for monthly invoice)
- hard_cap_fallback: boolean (if true, deny requests when (baseline+burst+grace) exhausted)

Acceptance criteria (testable):
1) Allocation and reporting:
   - When a plan upgrade or downgrade occurs, burst_pool_size adjusts immediately and the console shows prior/remaining burst credits with timestamps.
   - API /usage endpoint reports: baseline_used, burst_used, exemption_used, exemption_window_start, and decay_percentage for each tagged route.
2) Exemption behavior:
   - If a customer exceeds baseline+burst, subsequent requests are accepted and marked as "exempted" for the configured window; no overage invoices are created during that window.
   - Exemption decay applies per-minute and reduces the exemption entitlement so that partial periods are correctly prorated.
3) Reconciliation and invoicing:
   - For auto_charge_on_end=true accounts, at the end of the exemption window the system creates an invoice line item indicating original usage, exemption credits applied, discount applied (if any), and net charge.
   - For auto_charge_on_end=false accounts, usage is accumulated and only appears on the monthly invoice with clear line items for baseline, burst pool draw, exemption adjustments, and net overage.
   - Invoices expose tags that map usage back to request-level traces for finance and customer support.
4) Priority buckets:
   - Routes tagged as "priority" draw from reserved priority buckets. If reserved bucket exhausted and hard_cap_fallback=true, priority calls are routed to fallback model (as configured) and return a 429 with a specific error code and guidance.
5) Migrated customers:
   - Existing customers are migrated with a deterministic default burst_pool_size (algorithm documented) and receive an onboarding email with their initial values. No customer should see an unexpected immediate charge as a result of migration.
6) Observability & billing accuracy:
   - Dashboard exposes per-account and per-route burst utilization and projected month-end overage with a confidence band.
   - Billing reconciliation reports (internal) agree with invoice lines for >= 99.9% of accounts in a sample of 1000 accounts.

Edge cases and anti-abuse:
- Bots or repeated short requests: rate-limit integration required so burst consumption cannot be used to amplify abuse.
- Very long exemption windows: cap exemption_window_hours at 168 hours (7 days).
- Retroactive refunds: if a reconciliation error is detected, a reversible credit mechanism exists and finance can issue adjustments; automatic refunds require a separate approval flow.

Data model notes (for ENG):
- Add fields to usage ledger records: burst_bucket_id, exemption_window_id, decay_pct_at_consumption, priority_tag, reconciliation_state.
- Maintain immutability for ledger entries; reconciliation should create adjustment entries rather than editing consumed lines.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha (internal): 2 accounts in Dedicated + 5 hosted beta customers. Validate logs, traces, and invoices.
- Beta (opt-in): up to 200 accounts; collect customer feedback and adjust defaults.
- GA (auto-migrate): migrate accounts with low volatility first, then high volatility cohorts in waves.

Monitoring and success metrics:
- Support ticket volume for burst/overage issues (target: -60%).
- Fraction of invoices requiring manual adjustments (target: <0.5% of invoices).
- Reconciliation delta vs ledger (target: <0.1% of billed amount).

Dependencies and action items for other teams:
- ENG: implement ledger fields, API endpoints (/billing/usage, /billing/burst-config), and console UI hooks.
- Console: design prioritization UI for route tags and burst allocations.
- Finance: define invoice line item taxonomy and adjustment flows.
- Legal/Security: review terms for grace windows and potential usage disputes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Revenue leakage if exemption windows too generous: mitigate with decay curves and hard caps.
- Confusing customer UX: mitigate by shipping clear console visualizations and onboarding emails.
- Complex reconciliation: build internal reports early and test extensively in alpha.

Open questions (to resolve during discovery):
- Default burst_pool_size algorithm: historical 90th percentile of daily peak vs fixed percentage of monthly quota?
- Decay curve choices: do customers need exponential decay for some verticals?
- Should exemption windows be extendable based on billing standing or negotiated enterprise terms?

Acceptance sign-off checklist (for PM/Product Ops):
- [ ] Documentation for defaults and migration algorithm published to help center.
- [ ] API spec reviewed and approved by ENG.
- [ ] Finance run two end-to-end mock invoicing runs with synthetic data and confirm mapping.
- [ ] Console mockups validated by at least two customers in beta.
